extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies and NEPA practitioners preparing environmental impact statements and environmental assessments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing NEPA environmental impact statements and environmental assessments, including public participation, scheduling, scope/tiering, document content, format, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall notify persons, agencies, and organizations that may be interested or affected by the proposed action using methods such as: (A) personal notice or mail; (B) following affected State or Tribe's public notification procedures; (C) publication in local newspapers; (D) other local media; (E) potentially interested community organizations, including small business associations; (F) publication in newsletters; (G) direct mailing to owners and occupants of nearby or affected property; (H) posting of notification on- and off-site; and (I) electronic media (e.g., a project or agency website, dashboard, email list, or social media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should establish email notification lists or similar methods for the public to easily request electronic notifications for a proposed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of EIS, comments, and underlying documents (FOIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make environmental impact statements, the comments received, and any underlying documents available to the public pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552) and without charge to the extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access consistent with FOIA and remove barriers to public review as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meetings and hearings — when and how to hold them
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall hold or sponsor public hearings, public meetings, or other opportunities for public engagement whenever appropriate or in accordance with statutory/regulatory requirements or agency NEPA procedures. Agencies may conduct hearings/meetings by electronic communication except where another format is required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining format (in-person, virtual, formal hearing, listening session), agencies shall consider needs of affected communities; allow comments electronically, by regular mail, or other appropriate methods; make a draft environmental document available at least 15 days in advance when it is the subject of a public hearing or meeting unless meeting is for development of the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency engagement in preparing NEPA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall make diligent efforts to engage the public in preparing and implementing their NEPA procedures (§1507.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public engagement should inform agency procedures for implementing NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and schedules requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies shall set deadlines and schedules appropriate to individual actions or types of actions to ensure sound NEPA reviews are conducted efficiently and expeditiously, consistent with this section and §1506.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead agency should establish schedules in consultation with joint lead, cooperating, participating agencies, and applicants as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for Environmental Assessments and Environmental Impact Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall complete environmental assessments within 1 year and environmental impact statements within 2 years unless the lead agency extends the deadline in writing, with the new deadline providing only so much additional time as is necessary to complete the assessment or statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions should be in writing and, as applicable, in consultation with any applicant and other affected agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement points for deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines are measured from the sooner of: (i) date the agency determines NEPA requires an EIS or EA; (ii) date agency notifies an applicant the application to establish a right-of-way is complete; or (iii) date agency issues a notice of intent. Deadlines end at specific completion points for EAs and EISs (e.g., publication of EA, issuance of notice of availability for final EIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1501.10(b)(3)–(4) for detailed measurement start/end events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting missed deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each lead agency shall annually submit the report to Congress on any missed deadlines for environmental assessments and environmental impact statements required by section 107(h) of NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal tracking to support accurate annual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead agency schedule development and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead agency shall develop a schedule for completion of environmental impact statements and environmental assessments and any authorizations required to carry out the action; set milestones for all environmental reviews, permits, and authorizations required for implementation; and do so in consultation with applicants and cooperating/participating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedules should be based on the lead agency's expertise reviewing similar actions; all agencies with milestones should take measures to meet the schedule and escalate unresolved disputes to appropriate officials promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider in determining schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead agency may consider: (1) potential for environmental harm; (2) size of the proposed action; (3) state of the art of analytic techniques; (4) degree of public need for the proposed action; (5) number of persons and agencies affected; (6) availability of relevant information; (7) degree of substantial dispute about size, location, nature, or consequences; (8) time limits imposed by law/regulation/Executive order/court; (9) time necessary for government-to-government Tribal consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these factors to tailor realistic schedules that reflect complexity and stakeholder needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule content for Environmental Impact Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule for EISs shall include milestones: (1) publication of the notice of intent; (2) issuance of the draft EIS; (3) public comment period on the draft EIS (consistent with §1506.10); (4) issuance of the final EIS; and (5) issuance of the record of decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these milestones publicly and track completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule content for Environmental Assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule for EAs shall include milestones: (1) decision to prepare an EA; (2) issuance of the draft EA, where applicable; (3) the public comment period on the draft EA, where applicable (consistent with §1501.5); and (4) issuance of the final EA and decision on whether to issue a FONSI or notice of intent to prepare an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transparency about EA milestones as with EIS schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of person to expedite NEPA process
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may designate a person (such as the project manager or a person in the agency's office with NEPA responsibilities) to expedite the NEPA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation can clarify responsibility and help meet schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and revision of schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: For EISs, agencies shall make schedules for completing the NEPA process publicly available (e.g., on their website). If agencies make subsequent changes to the schedule, they shall publish revisions and explain the basis for substantial changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep public informed of both schedules and substantive schedule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic environmental documents — purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may prepare programmatic environmental documents (EISs or EAs) to evaluate environmental effects of policies, programs, plans, or groups of related activities; such documents should be relevant to agency decisions and timed to coincide with meaningful points in agency planning and decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use programmatic documents to conduct broad evaluations, evaluate widely applicable measures, or avoid duplicative analysis for individual actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to evaluate programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing programmatic documents, agencies may find it useful to evaluate proposals: (i) geographically (actions in same general location); (ii) thematically/by sector (actions with relevant similarities); or (iii) by stage of technological development (programs for new technologies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the evaluation approach appropriate to the program's nature to prevent premature commitment of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency actions appropriate for programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions appropriate include: (i) programs, policies, or plans (including land use/resource management plans); (ii) regulations; (iii) national or regional actions; (iv) actions with multiple stages/phases part of an overall plan/program; (v) a group of projects or related types of projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider programmatic documents for actions that benefit from broad-level analysis to streamline later site-specific reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ scoping and tiering for programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should, as appropriate, employ scoping, tiering, and other methods to describe relationships between programmatic documents and related individual actions and to avoid duplication and delay. The programmatic document shall identify any decisions or categories of decisions the agency anticipates making in reliance on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify anticipated reliance decisions to guide later tiered analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an existing EIS, EA, or programmatic document is relevant to a later action, agencies may employ tiering to avoid duplication, focus on issues not fully addressed earlier, and exclude issues already decided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tiering to concentrate subsequent analyses on site-, phase-, or stage-specific conditions and reasonably foreseeable effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiered document content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing a tiered document that follows a programmatic or earlier review, the tiered document shall discuss the relationship to the previous review, summarize and incorporate by reference issues discussed in the broader document, concentrate on issues specific to the subsequent action, analyze site-/phase-/stage-specific conditions and effects, provide public engagement opportunities consistent with the document type and location, and state where the earlier document is publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly cite and incorporate earlier analyses while focusing the tiered document on new, decision-relevant issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: When tiering is appropriate (sequencing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiering is appropriate when: (i) from programmatic/plan/policy EIS/EA to a program/plan/policy statement or to a site-specific statement/assessment of narrower scope; or (ii) from an EIS/EA on a specific action at an early stage to a subsequent statement/assessment at a later stage (e.g., need and site selection to environmental mitigation), when it helps focus on issues ripe for decision and exclude issues already decided or not yet ripe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tiering to sequence reviews logically as project development progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluation of programmatic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where judicial review was available for a programmatic document, agencies may rely on its analysis in subsequent documents as follows: (1) within 5 years and without additional review unless substantial new circumstances or information; (2) after 5 years, the agency shall reevaluate the analysis and underlying assumptions, briefly document its reevaluation and explain why the analysis remains valid considering new substantial information or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reevaluations to justify continued reliance on older programmatic analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — when permitted and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall incorporate material (planning studies, analyses, or other relevant information) into environmental documents by reference when it will cut down on bulk without impeding agency and public review. Agencies shall cite the incorporated material, briefly describe its content, and briefly explain its relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not incorporate by reference unless the material is reasonably available for review (e.g., publicly accessible website) throughout the time allowed for comment; provide digital references or hyperlinks; do not incorporate proprietary data that is not available for review and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of environmental impact statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of an EIS is to serve as an action-forcing device by ensuring agencies consider the environmental effects of their action in decision making, so that NEPA policies and goals are infused into ongoing federal programs and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EISs must meaningfully influence agency decisions by surfacing environmental effects and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and fair discussion and focus on reasonable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs shall provide full and fair discussion of significant effects and inform decision makers and the public of reasonable alternatives that would avoid or minimize adverse effects or enhance the quality of the human environment. Agencies shall focus on important environmental issues and reasonable alternatives and reduce paperwork and accumulation of extraneous background data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on decision-relevant issues and avoid lengthy irrelevant background material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness, clarity, and evidentiary support
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs shall be concise, clear, and to the point, and shall be supported by evidence that the agency has made necessary environmental analyses. An EIS is more than a disclosure document; agencies shall use EISs with other relevant material to plan actions, involve the public, and make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analyses are traceable and supported by appropriate data and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS implementation constraints — not encyclopedic and proportionate discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs shall not be encyclopedic; discuss effects in proportion to their significance with only brief discussion of unimportant issues. EISs shall be analytical, concise, and no longer than necessary to comply with NEPA and these regulations; length should be proportional to potential environmental effects and the scope and complexity of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize resources toward significant effects; summarize or reference less important material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement on alternatives and agency commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: EISs shall state how alternatives considered and decisions based on them will or will not achieve requirements of NEPA and other environmental laws; the range of alternatives shall encompass those to be considered by the decision maker; agencies shall not commit resources prejudicing selection of alternatives; EISs shall assess environmental impacts rather than justify decisions already made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pre-decisional actions that foreclose reasonable alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall use scoping, an early and open process, to determine the scope of issues for analysis in an EIS, identifying important issues and eliminating unimportant issues. Scoping should begin as soon as practicable after the proposal is sufficiently developed for agency consideration and may include pre-application procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scoping to focus analysis and identify participants and key issues early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping outreach and inviting participation
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing an EIS, agencies shall facilitate notification to persons and agencies who may be interested or affected, may hold scoping meetings or publish scoping information, and shall invite participation of likely affected Federal, State, Tribal, and local agencies and governments as cooperating or participating agencies, any applicant, and other likely affected or interested persons (including those not in accord with the action), unless a limited exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure broad and inclusive outreach to identify issues and cooperating entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional scoping responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of scoping the lead agency shall: (1) identify and eliminate from detailed study issues not important or covered by prior review; (2) allocate assignments among lead and cooperating agencies, with lead agency retaining responsibility; (3) indicate any publicly available EAs and other EISs related but not part of the scope; (4) identify other environmental review, authorization, and consultation requirements to prepare analyses concurrently; (5) indicate relationship between timing of environmental analyses and agencies' tentative planning and decision-making schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document scoping outcomes and responsibilities to avoid duplication and coordinate concurrent reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of intent published in the Federal Register shall include, as appropriate: (1) purpose and need; (2) preliminary description of proposed action and alternatives to be considered; (3) brief summary of expected effects; (4) anticipated permits and authorizations; (5) schedule for decision-making; (6) description of public scoping process; (7) request for comment on alternatives and effects and on relevant information/studies; (8) contact information for agency person who can answer questions; (9) identification of cooperating/participating agencies and information they require; (10) a unique identification number for tracking purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the notice of intent to provide essential info enabling meaningful public and agency participation; reference the ID number on all documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of withdrawal or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency withdraws, cancels, or otherwise ceases consideration of a proposed action before completing a final EIS, the agency shall publish a notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public is informed when proposals are discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall revise scoping determinations if substantial changes are made later in the proposed action, or if important new circumstances or information arise that bear on the proposal or its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update scoping and disclose revisions when new information or changes alter issues for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of EIS preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should commence EIS preparation as close as practicable to the time the agency is developing or receives a proposal so the final statement can be included in any recommendation or report; the statement shall be prepared early enough to serve as an important practical contribution to decision-making and not be used to rationalize decisions already made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a) for agency projects prepare EIS at feasibility stage; (b) for applications, commence as soon as practicable after receiving complete application; (c) for adjudication, final EIS normally precedes final staff recommendation; (d) for informal rulemaking, draft EIS shall normally accompany proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall prepare EISs using an interdisciplinary approach that ensures integrated use of natural and social sciences and the environmental design arts; the disciplines of preparers shall be appropriate to scope and issues identified in scoping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble teams with the technical expertise necessary to address identified issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for final EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of final EISs, not including citations or appendices, shall not exceed 150 pages except for proposals of extraordinary complexity, which shall not exceed 300 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep narrative concise and use appendices for supporting material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style for EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall write EISs in plain language and should use, as relevant, appropriate visual aids or charts so decision makers and the public can readily understand statements. Agencies should employ writers of clear prose or editors to write, review, or edit statements, which shall be based upon analysis and supporting data from the natural and social sciences and the environmental design arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize clarity and accessibility; use visual aids where they clarify analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft, final, and supplemental statement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall generally prepare EISs in two stages (draft and final) and, where necessary, supplement them. Draft EISs must meet requirements for final statements to the fullest extent practicable; final EISs shall consider and respond to comments. Agencies shall prepare supplements when substantial changes to the proposed action or substantial new circumstances/information arise, and file supplements as draft and final unless Council approves alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a draft is so inadequate as to preclude meaningful analysis, prepare and publish a supplemental draft of the appropriate portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluation for supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may reevaluate an EIS to determine whether a supplement is required under the supplement criteria and should document its finding consistent with agency NEPA procedures or, if necessary, prepare a supplemental EA and FONSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reevaluation to assess whether new information or changes trigger supplemental analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended EIS format
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall use a format that encourages good analysis and clear presentation; agencies should use the standard format unless a more effective format is determined: (1) Cover; (2) Summary; (3) Table of contents; (4) Purpose of and need for action; (5) Alternatives including the proposed action; (6) Affected environment and environmental consequences; (7) Appendices (including summary of scoping and list of preparers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a different format, include the substantive elements described in §§1502.11–1502.19 in an appropriate way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS cover shall not exceed one page and shall include: (a) list of lead, joint lead, and cooperating agencies; (b) title of proposed action and location (State(s), county(ies) or other jurisdiction); (c) name, address, telephone number for contact person; (d) designation as draft/final/supplement; (e) one-paragraph abstract; (f) date by which agency must receive comments (computed with EPA under §1506.10); (g) identification number from notice of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep cover brief but include key contact and tracking information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each EIS shall contain a summary that adequately and accurately summarizes the statement, including major conclusions, any disputed issues raised by agencies and public, any issues to be resolved, key differences among alternatives, and identification of the environmentally preferable alternative(s). The summary shall be written in plain language and normally should not exceed 15 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary to present the core findings and tradeoffs for decision makers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and need statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall include a statement that briefly summarizes the underlying purpose and need for the proposed agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state why the agency is proposing the action to frame alternative development and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives section as the heart of the EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: The alternatives section should identify reasonably foreseeable environmental effects of the proposed action and alternatives in comparative form, sharply define issues for decision makers and the public, and provide a clear basis for choice among options. Agencies shall: (a) rigorously explore and objectively evaluate reasonable alternatives and briefly discuss reasons for eliminating alternatives from detailed study; (b) discuss each alternative in detail including the proposed action; (c) include the no action alternative; (d) identify the agency's preferred alternative(s) in the draft and final (unless prohibited by law); (e) include appropriate mitigation measures not already in the proposed action or alternatives; (f) identify the environmentally preferable alternative(s) and explain that it maximizes environmental benefits (e.g., addressing climate change, protecting historic/cultural/Tribal/natural resources, minimizing damage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider a reasonable range of alternatives (not every conceivable one), and explicitly identify the environmentally preferable and preferred alternatives with supporting analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected environment description
rubrics_metrics.description: The EIS shall succinctly describe the environment of the area(s) to be affected by the alternatives, including reasonably foreseeable environmental trends and planned actions in the area. Agencies shall use high-quality information, including reliable data, models, and Indigenous Knowledge, to describe reasonably foreseeable trends including anticipated climate-related changes; when information is incomplete or unavailable provide relevant information consistent with §1502.21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description should be no longer than necessary to understand relevant environment and effects; data and analyses commensurate with importance of the effect; avoid useless bulk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental consequences section — basis for comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: This section forms the scientific and analytic basis for comparisons under the alternatives section; it shall consolidate discussions of elements required by NEPA that are within the scope and as much of other required elements as necessary. Comparisons shall be based on reasonably foreseeable effects and their significance, focusing on significant or important effects. The no action alternative should serve as the baseline for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus analysis on significant effects and use no action as baseline to compare alternatives.
